newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU rapeseed crop holds key to July/Sept crush.
newsitem.headline: EU rapeseed crop holds key to July/Sept crush.

text.p: An ample European Union rapeseed crop in the third quarter of 1997 may help boost EU oilseeds crush volumes to 6.16 million tonnes, up two percent from the same 1996 period, Oil World newsletter said.

First arrivals of domestic rapeseed from the 97/98 harvest may more than offset a shortfall in sunseed processing amid lower imports, while soybean crushings in the three months should be stable, the independent publication said.
Its EU July/Sept crush forecast was as follows -- soybeans 3.15 million tonnes (3.14 million 1996), sunseed 890,000 (990,000), rapeseed 1.80 million (1.57), others 320,000 (330,000).
Soybean stocks had been built in the EU in May and June when Brazilian arrivals peaked but worsening crush margins had now caused a relative slow-down in acitivities, Oil World said.
The EU's April/June 1997 soy crush had been 3.69 million tonnes (3.42 million a year earlier).

Rapeseed crops were looking favourable in France, Germany and Britain, although yields in France and Germany may be down due to frost damage and Germany's official area estimates are not yet known, Oil World added.
It tentatively estimated the EU 1997 rapeseed crop at 7.9 million tonnes, up 800,000 tonnes from last year. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
